From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health - leadership recap & procurement path (post-discovery)

Alexandra / Tom — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery with the Aurora leadership group and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Key pain points (heard today)
- High latency on batch claims enrichment pipelines; current on-prem system spikes during EOB runs and blocks daily SLAs.
- Rising per-token cost from current vendor and inconsistent availability during month-end peaks.
- PHI/data residency constraints: most records must remain within the east-us region and meet SOC 2 + HITRUST expectations.

Desired outcomes / success metrics
- Reduce median inference latency for the enrichment task to <120ms per request at 99th percentile.
- Lower per-unit cost by at least 30% vs current monthly run-rate after caching/batching optimizations.
- Pilot completed within 6 weeks, demonstrating compliance and performance on a 10k-record tranche.

Procurement path we discussed (recommended)
- Pilot (60-day): Dedicated capacity + limited dataset (east-us). SOW for scope + acceptance criteria — Redwood provides SOC 2 evidence and a data handling addendum.
- Production: Transition to a 12-month reserved capacity contract (Dedicated) or private deployment depending on audit/legal outcomes.
- Billing: Aurora prefers PO + net-45 for production; pilot to be covered by a short-term MSA addendum.

Open risks / blockers (leadership-level)
- Legal signoff on data residency and encryption at rest (KMS/HSM details).
- Procurement needing exact pricing buckets for committed tokens vs burst.
- Integration window for the claims pipeline (ops wants a canary deployment strategy).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood: Share post-call notes, draft pilot SOW, and SOC 2 pack — attached. (Jasmine) — by EOD Thu 2026-10-01.
2) Aurora: Confirm procurement contact and preferred PO workflow + any legal redlines to watch. (Alexandra / Tom) — by Mon 2026-10-05.
3) Redwood Solutions: Produce a high-level dev runbook for the canary plan and expected infra changes. (Karthik) — by Fri 2026-10-08.

Attachments: 2026-09-30-aurora-postcall-notes.pdf (post-call notes + acceptance criteria)

If this aligns, I suggest a short procurement sync next week to walk the SOW and pricing buckets with Procurement and Legal on the call. Please flag anything I missed.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Health - leadership recap & procurement path (post-discovery)

Thanks, Jasmine — this is helpful and comprehensive. A few clarifications from the Aurora side: 

- Timeline: leadership wants the pilot started within 4–6 weeks, so your 60-day pilot fits but we need the SOW this week to keep legal on track.
- Compliance: please include evidence for SOC 2 Type II and a brief on how you handle PHI (encryption keys, separation of logs, vendor access controls). Can you also confirm east-us-only hosting for the pilot?
- Procurement: we use standard PO with net-45 for production. For the pilot, Procurement prefers a short-term invoice rather than a PO; they asked me to loop them in — included above.

On risks, two items to call out to your leadership: 1) our security team has a standing requirement for a third-party pen test within the last 12 months if the provider will process PHI, and 2) we will want an auditable audit-log window (90 days minimum).

Quick note: tagging my legal lead (Tom) — if there are known contract clauses that typically slow you down, flag them now so we can prioritize review.

Best,
Alexandra
Sr. Director, Digital Transformation
Aurora Health
